newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland drops plan for change in road tax.
newsitem.headline: Poland drops plan for change in road tax.

text.p: The Polish government on Tuesday decided to drop plans to include the current road tax in the price of petrol as of 1997 because of inflationary concerns, the government press office said.

It said in a statement that the move would have worked against the government's anti-inflationary policy because it would have resulted in a gasoline price rise of between seven and eight groszes, which could boost prices of other products.
"The government sees no possibility of including the road tax in the price of liquid fuels from January 1997," the statement said.

The government wanted to change the way the tax for car owners, known as the road tax, is collected because under current regulations, it is widely evaded. The tax is currently collected by local governments.
The statement also confirmed government plans to liberalise gasoline prices, now controlled by the finance ministry, only when world oil prices go down.
Poland originally planned to free prices of domestically produced gasoline by the end of 1996.
But faced with mounting world oil prices, the government has delayed the liberalisation, fearing it would jeopardise its plans to cut inflation to 17 percent this year from 21.6 percent in 1995.
